definition: The practiced, barely-perceptible gesture of compliance performed by lower-tier residents when passing through Ferrogate Security checkpoints — a micro-expression of deference engineered to satisfy behavioral recognition algorithms without visibly appearing submissive to onlookers.
origin: Street slang, Old Harbor; named for Ferrogate Security's omnipresent checkpoint infrastructure
usage: Tier 1–3 residents navigating checkpoints; discussed with dark humor and weary familiarity
example: He didn't even think about it anymore — the Ferrogate curtsy was muscle memory, same as breathing, same as keeping his eyes down.
